title: PCTE Protocol for VLP Enumeration
author: Ken Stedman
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.eaubaew
materials: When the virus particles have been extracted from the suspension, vacuum is released and 0.5 mL of a 1:400 SYBR Gold solution is added to the funnel. The SYBR Gold solution is prepared using SM buffer (100mM NaCl, 10mM MgCl 2 and 50mM Tris-Base, adjusted to pH 8.0) or TE Buffer (10mM Tris-Base, 1mM EDTA, adjusted to pH 8.0) to maintain a pH between 7.5 and 8.3, as pH outside this range adversely affects fluorescence of the SYBR Gold stain (Invitrogen).

steps.title: Assemble support filter
steps.instruction: Place a 200 nm pore, 25 mm diameter PVDF support filter onto a fritted glass base to provide an even surface for the downstream PCTE filter.

steps.title: Saturate support filter with water
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL virus‑free water onto the PVDF filter; apply slight vacuum suction if needed to draw the water into the support.

steps.title: Mount PCTE filter on support
steps.instruction: Carefully place the PCTE filter on top of the damp PVDF support, allowing a slight overlap to ease later removal.

steps.title: Clamp funnel onto assembly
steps.instruction: Mount the funnel onto the fritted base and clamp it securely so that both the support filter and the PCTE filter are held in place.

steps.title: Stain PCTE filter with Sudan black B
steps.instruction: While the filter stack is held between the fritted base and funnel, stain the PCTE filter with Sudan black B.

steps.title: Filter virus solution through membrane
steps.instruction: Add virus solution to the funnel and draw it through the stained PCTE filter at –70 kPa; filter at least 0.5 mL to ensure uniform coverage.

steps.title: Incubate filter in dark
steps.instruction: Allow the virus‑laden PCTE filter to stain for 10 minutes in the dark without applying vacuum.

steps.title: Apply SYBR Gold stain and rinse
steps.instruction: Re‑apply vacuum and draw SYBR Gold solution through the filter, then draw 1 mL SM or TE buffer through to rinse excess stain and dislodge any viruses stuck to the funnel walls. Keep vacuum on until the wash solution has completely passed through the filter.

substeps.instruction: Re‑apply vacuum and draw SYBR Gold solution through the filter.
Draw 1 mL SM or TE buffer through the filter.
Maintain vacuum until the wash solution fully exits the filter.

steps.title: Prepare antifade drops
steps.instruction: While the wash is proceeding, place a 5 µL drop of 1X antifade on a clean microscope slide and another 5 µL drop on a cover slip.

substeps.instruction: Place 5 µL 1X antifade on the slide surface.
Place 5 µL 1X antifade on the cover slip.

steps.title: Remove and dry filter
steps.instruction: When the wash is complete, release the vacuum, carefully lift the PCTE filter from the support with forceps, and gently wave it in the air a few times to dry.

substeps.instruction: Wave filter gently a few times to dry.

steps.title: Mount filter on slide with antifade
steps.instruction: Place the PCTE filter face‑up onto the 5 µL antifade drop on the slide.

steps.title: Place cover slip and press
steps.instruction: Lay the cover slip (with its 5 µL antifade drop) drop‑side down onto the filter, using no more than 5 µL antifade to avoid wrinkling, then gently press to remove air bubbles, smooth wrinkles, and fully saturate the filter.

substeps.instruction: Place cover slip drop‑side down on the filter.
Gently press to eliminate bubbles and wrinkles.

steps.title: Image slide promptly
steps.instruction: View the prepared slide by epifluorescence microscopy within a few hours; note that fading occurs even when stored at –20 °C.
